targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-592e (2026-06-01, supersedes V3-EXQ-592d) FAILed after correcting the 592d commit-entry-count defect. C1 baseline hold-rate fired, and both readiness predicates were measurable: ARM_1 score-margin blocks=1793, ARM_3 score-margin blocks=2088, ARM_2/3 nav-competence blocks=150 each. The failure is therefore not predicate silence. The informative result is that predicate firing did not produce discriminative committed-state occupancy under the script's hold-rate measure: all arms had hold_rate=1.0 and total_commits=0. Per-cell beta-elevation totals localise the issue further: score-margin gating can suppress BetaGate elevation when the latch is not elevated (ARM_1/3 beta-elevated fraction 0.0), but E3's rv-low committed-trajectory marker remains present because it is set upstream of BetaGate admission. Current code confirms the R-c predicates are wired to admission/elevation sites; no readiness-failure path releases an already-elevated bistable latch or clears E3 committed state. This is a direct integration/state-authority gap, not a clean conceptual falsification of MECH-090. Route to V3-EXQ-592f, a controlled state-machine probe of whether failed readiness can release/suppress an already-held committed state and recover when readiness returns.
learning_extracted: The predicates did fire: score-margin blocks were 1793 in ARM_1 and 2088 in ARM_3; nav-competence blocks were 150 in ARM_2 and 150 in ARM_3.
592e is more informative than 592d because it removed the structurally bad C1 entry-count predicate and exposed a predicate-to-state authority gap.
Score-margin gating can suppress BetaGate elevation when the latch is not yet elevated: per-cell totals give beta-elevated fraction 0.0 in ARM_1 and ARM_3.
The script's hold_rate counted e3._committed_trajectory, which E3 sets on rv-low selection upstream of BetaGate admission. That marker can stay at 1.0 even when beta elevation is suppressed.

In bistable mode, score-margin admission is consulted only on the not-yet-elevated transition tick; nav readiness can emit block diagnostics on rv-low selections but is still only AND-composed into the elevation call.

No current readiness-failure path calls beta_gate.release() or clears the E3 committed marker; release exists through separate mechanisms such as hippocampal completion, urgency interrupt, V_s invalidation, relief/safety, contextual safety, and SD-034 closure.

The next experiment must be a controlled commitment-state transition probe that starts already committed, forces predicate failure, measures beta/e3 state occupancy and release transitions, and then restores readiness to test recovery.

acceptance_criteria.C3_nav_competence_release_authority: nav_competence_blocks > 0 and beta_elevated_fraction decreases by >= 0.5 from baseline OR e3_committed_pointer_fraction decreases by >= 0.5 from baseline OR decommit_transition_count >= 1
acceptance_criteria.C4_conjunction_authority: both direct gate-failure counters > 0 and Stage D suppression is at least as strong as the strongest single-gate suppression
acceptance_criteria.C5_recovery: after gates restore, beta_elevated_fraction rises to at least 0.8 of baseline; if no suppression occurred earlier, recovery is not evaluable and overall cannot PASS
acceptance_criteria.C6_no_vacuity: forced perturbations must cross thresholds; otherwise INVALID / harness failure, not FAIL

final_concise_verdict: 592e showed that MECH-090 predicates fire but lack demonstrated authority over commitment maintenance/release. 592f must directly test whether failed readiness can release or suppress an already-held committed state, and whether commitment can recover when readiness returns.
